title: Wise Words
subtitle: WITH MARCO REYES  ·  STORY NIGHT

segments.head: TONIGHT: PAULA AND THE PEAK
segments.author: Wise Words
lines: Good evening, everyone.
I'm Marco Reyes, and this is Wise Words.
Tonight's story is about Paula Jessup, a grocery store cake decorator in Ogden, Utah.
At fifty-two, she decided to climb the tallest mountain in Utah.

segments.head: CHAPTER 1: SOMEDAY
segments.quote: If one does not know to which port one is sailing, no wind is favorable.
segments.author: Seneca
lines: For years Paula said someday. Someday I'll get in shape. Someday I'll see the view.
Her coworker Manny taped a card to the frosting fridge, from the Roman thinker Seneca:
If one does not know to which port one is sailing, no wind is favorable.
So Paula picked her port. Kings Peak. The second Saturday in August. She wrote it on the store calendar.

segments.head: CHAPTER 2: THE PACE
segments.author: Augustus
lines: On her first practice hike, Paula charged uphill like there was a sale on oxygen.
Ten minutes later she sat on a rock, purple, as a seventy-year-old man strolled past.
He smiled and said the Roman emperor Augustus had a motto:
Hasten slowly.
So Paula took small steps and breathed with every one. By June, she was passing him.

segments.head: CHAPTER 3: THE STORM
segments.quote: He who conquers others is strong; He who conquers himself is mighty.
segments.author: Lao Tzu
lines: In August, Paula started up before dawn.
One mile from the top, black clouds rolled in. Thunder. Then hail the size of sprinkles.
She wanted to push on. Then she remembered the Chinese thinker Lao Tzu:
He who conquers others is strong; He who conquers himself is mighty.
So Paula turned around, and ate a squashed sandwich in the rain.

segments.head: CHAPTER 4: THE PLAN
segments.quote: Luck is the residue of design.
segments.author: Branch Rickey
lines: At work, people said, tough luck, Paula.
Manny quoted Branch Rickey, the baseball man who signed Jackie Robinson:
Luck is the residue of design.
So all winter, Paula designed her luck. Stairs at lunch. A backpack full of flour bags. An earlier start.

segments.head: CHAPTER 5: THE RIDGE
segments.quote: Difficulties are things that show a person what they are.
segments.author: Epictetus
lines: Next August she tried again, and Manny came too.
Near the top was a ridge of loose rocks. Her legs shook. She said, that's it, I'm a cake lady.
Manny reminded her of Epictetus, a Greek teacher born a slave:
Difficulties are things that show a person what they are.
Paula stood up. Rock by rock, she found out she was a climber.

segments.head: CHAPTER 6: THE TOP
segments.quote: What we get from this adventure is just sheer joy. And joy is, after all, the end of life.
segments.author: George Mallory
lines: At ten in the morning, Paula stood on top of Utah.
She thought of George Mallory, the English climber who went to Everest a hundred years ago:
What we get from this adventure is just sheer joy. And joy is, after all, the end of life.
Paula laughed until she had to sit down. Back at the store, she baked a mountain cake that said: Someday was today.

segments.head: THAT'S TONIGHT'S STORY
segments.quote: Pick a port. Go slow. Know when to turn back. Plan your luck. Face the hard part. Enjoy the view.
segments.author: Marco Reyes
lines: That's tonight's story.
Pick a port. Go slow. Know when to turn back. Plan your luck. Face the hard part. Enjoy the view.
I climbed a mountain once. It was the stairs to my attic. I stopped halfway for a snack.
I'm Marco Reyes. Good night.
